component.name: Enclave
component.summary: Private messages without a phone number

description.p: Enclave is a messenger for chats, groups, photos, voice notes and calls that hides not only what you say but who you talk to and when.

ul.li: No phone number or email: your account is a key, and a username is optional.
Post-quantum encryption from the first message.
Traffic goes through Tor and the Nym mixnet, every message is the same size, and cover traffic hides when you are talking.
Servers are run by independent operators, and none of them can read messages, see your contacts or change your keys without being caught.
Your messages stay on your devices, encrypted, with an optional app lock and an emergency PIN.

description.p: On phones, nothing is drawn under the status bar, camera cut-out or navigation bar any more. Reopening the app no longer asks to set it up again while the vault is still starting, and a profile that doesn't open is never replaced. On Android the camera, the keystore and the pickers keep working after the app is reopened, and phones can lock with a fingerprint or face, no PIN needed. On the desktop the vault is started again when its network stops. Adding someone fetches their keys in parallel, the meeting code shows while it is made, and every slow step shows a bar with what it is doing. Copy log puts the app's log on the clipboard, to send when something goes wrong. The iPhone build passes the App Store's checks again.

Setting up an account over Tor is much faster: the vault key goes up in parallel, with its own progress bar and time left, and a stalled part is sent again instead of failing. Errors say why Tor isn't available. The spinner turns, "I already have Enclave" shows on every launch, and linking a device says it is getting a code.

Buttons work on the first click. Setting up an account shows each step. Linking a device keeps showing the same words, and a scanned link no longer runs off the screen. Phones don't ask for a passphrase when setting up.
Tor starts again on Android, where 0.1.1 couldn't set up an account ("no Tor"). The AUR source package builds.
Setting up an account no longer waits forever: Tor could fail to start on a new install, and the app now says so if it can't reach the server.
